properties.name: Red Bank Road (Grasmere–Langdale)
properties.reason: Official Lake District guidance describes this as single-track with very tight corners and unsuitable for lorries/caravans. Penfold is smaller, but it deserves an orange caution rather than being treated as an ordinary lane.

properties.name: Borrowdale B5289 (Keswick–Seatoller)
properties.reason: Narrow valley B-road with stone walls, buses, walkers and seasonal traffic. Penfold is a sensible size, but progress can be slow and meeting traffic needs care.

properties.name: Birker Fell road
properties.reason: Remote, narrow and steep with blind bends and little margin in places. Penfold fits, but this is an intentional scenic route rather than a relaxed shortcut.

properties.name: Martindale access road
properties.reason: Narrow dead-end Ullswater valley road with limited passing and turning options. Suitable only if you are happy reversing and have checked your destination.

properties.name: A592 Ullswater corridor
properties.reason: Main through route along Ullswater and a normal choice for campervans. Default suitable for Penfold unless temporary restrictions or severe weather apply.

properties.name: A66 Penrith–Keswick
properties.reason: Strategic trunk-road approach to the northern Lakes. Default green for Penfold; vastly preferable to minor-road shortcuts.

properties.name: Horseshoe Pass A542
properties.reason: Steep, exposed and bendy but a surfaced A-road. Penfold has no inherent dimensional issue; weather, motorcycles and cyclists are the bigger considerations.

properties.name: Nant-y-Moch reservoir road
properties.reason: Remote single-track reservoir road with limited passing and exposed sections. Penfold fits physically, but reversing and poor-weather confidence matter.

properties.name: A498 Aberglaslyn Pass
properties.reason: Narrow-feeling mountain A-road through rock and woodland, but regularly used by buses and visitor traffic. Penfold is suitable with normal care.
properties.evidence: National Park campervan guidance + road class

properties.name: Cwm Penmachno road
properties.reason: Narrow upland valley road with constrained passing and local traffic. Manageable in Penfold, but not a route to take casually on a satnav suggestion.

properties.name: Llyn Brianne reservoir roads
properties.reason: Remote reservoir roads are narrow and winding with limited passing. Penfold fits, but journey times are slow and reversing may be necessary.

properties.name: A5 Eryri corridor
properties.reason: Historic trunk route and main cross-North-Wales corridor, routinely used by coaches and HGVs. Default green for Penfold.

properties.name: A87 Broadford–Portree
properties.reason: Main Skye trunk road and normally straightforward for Penfold. In very high winds, Highland Council and Police Scotland have specifically warned campervans because exposed sections can be hazardous.

properties.name: A832 Wester Ross alternative corridor
properties.reason: Main alternative corridor around Wester Ross. Some stretches are narrower and slower, but NC500 guidance directs larger vehicles away from Bealach na Bà onto the easier alternative network.

properties.name: A837 Lochinver alternative
properties.reason: NC500 guidance recommends this main-road alternative rather than the B869 Drumbeg loop for larger vehicles. Straightforward for Penfold.

properties.name: B8008 Morar–Arisaig coastal road
properties.reason: Popular narrow coastal road with significant summer visitor-management and parking controls. Highland Council highlights emergency-access concerns; drive it deliberately and do not rely on roadside parking.

properties.name: A830 Road to the Isles
properties.reason: Modern strategic route from Fort William to Mallaig. Default green for Penfold; use this rather than unsigned coastal-lane alternatives when you want an easy journey.

properties.name: B884 Dunvegan–Neist Point
properties.reason: Narrow single-track road serving a very popular visitor destination. Congestion and repeated reversing are more likely than a dimensional problem for Penfold.

properties.name: A838 Durness–Tongue
properties.reason: Remote north-coast road with extensive single-track sections. Penfold is an appropriate size but passing-place etiquette and patience are essential.

properties.name: Kintyre east-coast single-track sections
properties.reason: VisitScotland specifically notes that sections of the Kintyre 66 east coast are single-track and can be challenging when towing. Penfold is smaller and should be fine with normal single-track discipline.
